text:
alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak i'm seeing a 10-15% p95 regression on 8xA100 tensor-parallel inference for the long-tail (seq_len 1024, batch 2).
mira: ugh, that matches a few customer reports. any obvious hotspot from traces?
alex: nvprof + our custom timers show increased wait on the all-reduce edges. compute kernels finish earlier but then sit ~3-6ms waiting for NCCL step.
jon: can you paste the timeline snippet? also which selector change landed?
alex: landed: prefer_fp16_fused_gemm_v2 when available; fallback logic now picks it even when chunking leads to extra small reduction calls. perf-bot posted a capture: https://perf.redwood/profiles/1775abc
perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: nsight_capture_1775012345.asc (summary: allreduce stalls increased, overlap dropped ~40%).
samir: small reductions across TP shards --> more allreduce ops = worse latency due to launch overhead and lack of overlap. maybe fusion got worse.
mira: do we have custom timer outputs for KV cache prefetch / invalidation? could be interacting with scheduling.
alex: pasted below (trimmed):
```
TIMER KVPrefetch:start 1775012345.12
TIMER KVPrefetch:duration 34.2ms
TIMER GEMM_fp16_v2:duration 18.1ms
TIMER AllReduce_wait:duration 5.8ms
TIMER GEMM_fp16_v1:duration 20.0ms
TIMER AllReduce_wait:duration 6.9ms
TIMER KernelLaunch_overhead:duration 0.9ms
```
jon: interesting — GEMM_v2 is slightly faster but increases number of AllReduce calls (smaller chunking). net effect: more overhead.
samir: that explains p95 tail. options: 1) adjust selector to favor fewer allreduce ops when total tokens > threshold, 2) batch adjacent sequences to align fusion, 3) increase async NCCL progress to overlap.
mira: can we repro with a synthetic trace and nsight timeline? i can run a 8-gpu run with nvprof/ncu for full timeline.
alex: i already ran a quick nsight: shows idle gaps between compute kernels matching NCCL steps. timeline attached in the profile link.
perf-bot: log snippet from ncu --target=timeline
```
Process: model_infer pid=8432
Stream 1: kernel GEMM_fp16_v2 [0:00:12.345] duration 18.1ms
Stream 2: kernel GEMM_fp16_v2 [0:00:12.370] duration 17.9ms
Stream 1: NCCL allreduce start [0:00:12.370]
Stream 1: NCCL allreduce end [0:00:12.380]
Stream 1: idle 5.8ms
```
jon: propose a quick experiment: add a heuristic in kernel selector that computes "estimated_allreduce_ops" and penalizes candidates that increase it by >10% for long sequences. alex, can you push a branch and we can run synthetic comparison?
alex: i'll drop a branch alex/selector-reduce-penalty and run 8GPU nightly replays.
samir: also try enabling ncclAsyncProgress=1 and set NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=0? maybe async progress reduces wait.
mira: be careful — async progress can increase CPU usage; need SRE signoff for Dedicated clusters.
alex: noted. for now i'll run local repro with nccl async progress on and the selector tweak.
perf-bot: queued job: nightly-replay-1775012345 on farm-gpu-08 (8xA100). status: queued
jon: if the selector tweak fixes it, also add a unit/regression test in perf harness that runs the seq_len 1024 case and asserts p95 delta < 2%.
alex: agreed. also adding a microbench measuring "allreduce_count" emitted by the planner.
samir: one more thought — KV cache prefetch invalidations might be increasing inter-GPU synchronization. check if prefetch triggers cross-shard consistency calls.
mira: good call. alex, add logs for KVInvalidation events to see if they line up with stalls.
alex: will do. timeline today -> tomorrow morning; i'll post results here.
jon: thanks. if we see fixes, we should roll back the change to prefer_fp16_fused_gemm_v2 until we have the selector penalty.
alex: for traceability i'll open an internal PR and link this thread. PR will include benchmark CSVs and nsight links.
perf-bot: job finished: nightly-replay-1775012345 status: failed (OOM on worker 4) — requeued with higher mem
alex: switching to smaller batch to avoid OOM and re-running.
mira: ping me when done, i'll run a diff of the new traces vs old.
alex: will post new profile link here when complete.
